newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK people place less trust in future leader - survey.
newsitem.headline: HK people place less trust in future leader - survey.

text.p: Hong Kong people are placing less trust in future leader Tung Chee-hwa amid concerns over his plans to curb freedoms in the territory after it reverts to China, according to a survey published on Monday.

The South China Morning Post, citing results of a survey it commissioned, reported that 25.2 percent of respondents believed they had "more trust" in Tung protecting Hong Kong's interests than when he was chosen in November.
This was a fall of 5.6 percent from a similar survey in April, the newspaper reported.
Altogether 41.7 percent of respondents in the survey, conducted last Monday to Wednesday by Asian Commercial Research (ACR), also said they had "less trust" in Tung.
The company polled 610 people via telephone.
In April Tung unveiled plans curbing protests and banning foreign funding for political groups in Hong Kong after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.

Under Sino-British treaties, Hong Kong was promised a high degree of self rule for the next 50 years under a "one country, two systems" formula.

But the survey also found that less people believed Tung, selected under close Chinese supervision in December to be Hong Kong's first post-handover leader, would uphold the "one country, two systems" pledge.
A total of 68.8 percent indicated they had confidence in the pledge, down from 75.9 percent in a similar survey in February.
ACR also found the Democratic Party in Hong Kong was still the most popular party in the territory.
If Hong Kong people were allowed to vote, the party would get 25.1 percent of the vote, far ahead of the second-placed, pro-China Liberal Party with 10.7 percent of the vote, the survey showed.

Democratic Party legislators, voted into office in popular elections in 1995, will lose their jobs from July 1 since China plans to disband the current legislative council and replace it with an interim chamber which it has helped form.
